itens.texto: The Windows installer is always in English, whatever the system language, with no language picker.
The Windows installer's finish page links to Ko-fi (https://ko-fi.com/orwell_eu) to support the project.
The macOS disk image has a "Support Orwell" link to Ko-fi next to the drag-to-Applications window.
The Windows .exe file description and the macOS system-audio permission prompt (screen sharing with sound) are now in English.

Desktop downloads go from 1.3.3 straight to 1.3.5, so desktop users also get everything in 1.3.4: Orwell is open source under the AGPL-3.0, with a "Source code" link in Settings > Help and diagnostics.
Orwell is now open source under the AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/magnuslab-sudo/orwell. A "Source code" link sits in Settings > Help and diagnostics and in the site footer.
The web app serves its source maps again.

Shared room: an account that rejoins through the room card from another device (browser to desktop app, for example) now stays in the channel and gets the echo of its own commit. Before, the commit was taken as lost after 10 s and retried once a minute, bumping the room epoch every time.
Desktop installers ship the licence (LICENSE), the copyright notice (NOTICE) and the third-party notices next to the program.
orwell.pt: support now goes through Ko-fi only (https://ko-fi.com/orwell_eu), with a "Support us" link next to Sign in and the Support link in the footer.

Replies. You can now reply to a specific message, like on Discord: the reply arrow in the hover bar, "Reply" in the context menu (long-press on mobile), R on a focused message, or swipe left on touch. A "Replying to {name}" bar sits above the composer with an "@ Mention" toggle (on by default; pings the original author through the normal mention path) and an X. Esc cancels, and a pending reply sticks to its room like a draft.

Replies show a one-line quote of the original (avatar, name, start of the text, "Image" or the file name). Clicking it jumps to the original and highlights it, pulling older history from the vault when needed. Deleted originals and originals this device never had say so instead of guessing.

Wire format unchanged: replies use the existing encrypted replyTo field, so 1.1.x to 1.3.2 clients see them as plain messages, and the server learns nothing new. Ticket rooms keep their own reply flow. Desktop and web now build the outgoing message with the same function.
Under reduced motion, the jump highlight (replies and search) now fades slower instead of snapping off.

SFU calls: a consume refused by the server is no longer final when the refusal can be a timing issue (app frozen for a few seconds, the other side rebuilding its media). Before, the person stayed silent until you left and rejoined. Only refusals that cannot change by waiting are final (incompatible codec, no seat, server full, wrong transport direction, no SFU, call caps). The rest retry at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 s, then wait for a signal: the person's voice.join or a new producer, an epoch change, or the receive transport reconnecting.

SFU calls: the client resyncs with the server's producer list (a repeated sfu.scope.join, no protocol change) after an "unknown" refusal, after a long main-thread stall, and after a slow sfu.consume reply. Dead producers are dropped, consumers whose producer.closed was lost are closed, and producers whose producer.new was lost are consumed. Two unknown-transport refusals in a row rebuild the call media.

Someone whose voice is still missing is no longer shown as "connected". The card says "in the call, no sound yet", with notice 453 ("You cannot hear {name} yet. The app is asking for the sound again."). Every refusal is logged with the server's code. Media still never flows without SFrame.

SFU calls no longer drop you with Error 448 the first time the media encryption is not ready. The sender retries the whole SFrame setup (key, worker ACK, transform) at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 8 s, and right away on every epoch change; when it succeeds the source goes live by itself. Nothing is sent unencrypted while it waits. Meanwhile the call stays up (you still hear everyone) and shows notice 449 ("Your microphone is not sending yet: preparing the encryption."). Error 448 only shows after the last attempt. Same for camera, screen, screen audio and music. Receivers without decryption now also retry on a timer, not only on the next commit.

A microphone that dies silently mid-call now comes back by itself. The app watches the capture track (ended, muted for 3 s), the audio context (not running for 2 s) and the voice chain worklet (processorerror, or no heartbeat for 3 s), reopens the same input device with the same processing and swaps the track into the same encrypted sender (replaceTrack), without leaving the call. If the mic keeps dying (more than 4 times a minute), the app stops and shows Error 452.
One NaN or Infinity in the voice chain (noise suppressor included) no longer silences your mic until you rejoin. The chain resets its state and drops one block instead.
An SFU send transport that never connects (or fails mid-call) is now logged and the call media is rebuilt automatically, up to 3 times a minute, keeping your capture.

Role order is now editable where you manage roles. The founder and admins can drag a role or use the Move up / Move down buttons (keyboard and screen-reader friendly, with a live announcement of the new position). The order is the signed rank, so every client shows the same order: member list groups, the role line under each name, profiles and role menus. Admin stays pinned on top. Delegated role managers can't reorder. New roles start at the bottom, for 1.1.x clients too. Desktop: added the reorder IPC; the app had no way to reorder before.

Settings > Notifications > Sounds: turning a sound type on now plays it, the way the master "Sounds" switch already plays the direct-message sound. Before, enabling any of the 27 per-type toggles was silent, so it looked like nothing had been enabled. Disabling stays silent. All 27 types are now covered end to end through the real sound engine with pre-1.2 stored preferences, and in real Chromium with an analyser on the output.

Chat: opening a room no longer scrolls on its own. Switching rooms inside the same channel was treated as "new messages arrived", so the timeline smooth-scrolled from the top to the bottom or, coming from a bigger room, didn't scroll at all. Scroll state is now keyed on channel + room, each room restores its own position, and returns to the bottom if you left it there.

Chat: images and YouTube thumbnails reserve their final box before decoding. Image dimensions are read from the data: URL header (PNG, GIF, WebP, JPEG incl. EXIF orientation); YouTube cards get a fixed 480px width. Rooms used to open 400-1500px above the bottom once images finished decoding. Following new messages at the bottom is now instant and happens before paint; only scrolling up detaches you from the bottom, and an image finishing loading keeps you pinned.

Chat: removed the horizontal scrollbar above the composer (always visible on Windows). The hidden tooltip of the rightmost message action overflowed the timeline by ~53px; it now opens towards the inside.

Fixed freezes after someone joins a big channel (calls cutting out, the app hanging for seconds). The vault was rewritten in full for every live event; it is now written at most once a second for live application messages, while commits, Welcomes, catch-up, sends and flush still write at once. One join in a 120-member room went from 116 vault writes to 9; in Chromium at 4x CPU slowdown with a 10.7 MB vault, main-thread busy time per join dropped from 35-41 s to 4.4 s and the longest task from 5.1-13.4 s to 0.64-0.68 s. A crash loses at most the last second of events, which the server sends again.

Channel admins no longer stall after each join. Every send writes the whole vault before the frame leaves (so the ratchet never reuses a generation after a crash), and the cascade an admin sends to each newcomer (one role.assign per role holder, categories, rooms) was ~100 sends: 101 full vault writes and ~6 s of CPU per join with a 13 MB vault, holding the group while the next commit and the media key waited. The cascade is now encrypted in one go, the vault is written once after the last message, and the frames go out in the same order: 8-9 writes per join, and the room settles in 5-6 s instead of 13-14 s.

Web: every vault write ran a JS FNV hash twice over the whole file, on the page thread inside the IndexedDB transaction (18 s of 54 s of writes with an 11 MB vault at 4x CPU slowdown). The tab-ownership stamp now hashes 4 KB from each end plus the size. Old full-hash stamps still verify, so updating mid-session keeps ownership.

Checkboxes: the check glyph is now centred in its box at every display scale. It was an 11px clip-path box sitting 1/3px low and pixel-snapped on its own, so at 125% and 150% it drifted up to 1.5 device px (most visible on "Remember session" at sign-in on Windows). The ::before now fills the box and draws the check as a centred mask. Measured in Chromium and Electron at 1x, 1.25x and 1.5x.

Members without a display name (or whose profile hasn't reached you yet) now show the first word of their address, capitalised, instead of "No name": @ginvodra-sastybis-…:orwell.pt reads as Ginvodra. Address-derived names are rendered in italics in the secondary colour with a "From the address" title, so they can't pass for a chosen name. Two unnamed accounts on the same screen sharing a first word both get their second word too. Applies everywhere a name is shown, federated addresses included.

Reworked the report window. Three steps (Reason, Review, Send) with a step indicator. The reason step shows the reported message or person on top, with the note, good-faith box and contact under the reasons. Review shows the reported message with a red bar, the context in dimmer cards, a summary of everything that leaves the device, and the long addresses behind "Show addresses". On phones it is a bottom sheet with the button pinned above the safe area. Fixes the time running into names and badges, addresses breaking lines and list numbers over the text.

Reports inbox (Channel properties > Moderation) now has the app's look: one card per report with the reason, day, reported person, channel, room and a "Verified" / "Not verified" proof badge, the note, and the messages with the reported one marked.

Founder copies now reach every device of the founder's account. The device with the account key opens the copy and passes it, already open, to your other devices over the encrypted account channel. A paired device shows "N reports are waiting" until then, instead of "Nobody reported anything". The server learns nothing new. Both devices need this version.

Reports: message menu or member menu > "Report…". Eight reasons, an optional note and contact, and a preview of exactly what leaves the device before you send. Reported messages carry the author's autoria signature, so the server and the channel founder can verify who wrote them. Attachments go as name, type and size only, never the file.

Founder copy: when the report comes from a channel and the founder is in it, the founder gets a sealed copy in Channel properties > Moderation, 1 to 6 hours later. No reporter address, no reporter messages, and only the day of the report.

Account suspension (server): an operator can suspend an account until a set day or until review. The gateway and key package endpoints refuse it. Nothing is automatic and no report count suspends anyone. The suspended account sees the full notice (measure, duration, scope, facts, rule, redress) and can ask for a review.
The reporter gets the decision ("account suspended" or "no action") in the notification bell.
Terms and privacy: new Reports section, a single contact address (orwell.eu@proton.me), and the review deadline set to 30 days.

Security: SFU calls no longer publish media that is not end-to-end encrypted. The SFrame transform is attached before the sender is negotiated (mediasoup onRtpSender), and the media key (plus the worker ACK on Firefox and Safari) must be ready before a producer is created. If encryption cannot be set up, the producer is closed locally and on the server before any RTP goes out: for the mic you leave the call; for camera, screen, screen audio and music only that source is dropped. Error 448 says which. Reported by an external audit of 1.1.0 (SEC-02).
Security: SFU calls no longer play a stream whose decryption could not be installed. It stays paused on the server instead of reaching the decoder.

Security: when someone is removed from the channel's MLS group mid-call, their media keys are wiped in both decryptors (main thread and worker, with ACK), and their streams are paused on the server and dropped from what you hear and see, whatever their roster presence. People re-seated on a new MLS leaf keep being heard. Reported by an external audit of 1.1.0 (SEC-03).

Security (server): one account per socket. The gateway refuses auth.begin and auth.finish on a socket that is already signed in (already-authenticated, fatal). A second login on the same socket used to inherit the first account's channel set (AUTH-02).

Security (server): redeeming an invite no longer grants a seat. invite.redeem only forwards invite.request to connected members; the seat comes from the directed Welcome. channel.groupinfo.take grants a 2-minute temporary seat that accepts exactly one external commit for that channel, and becomes a subscription only when that commit is accepted as the epoch's commit (INV-01).

Security (server): redemption ceilings. Key packages are capped at 8 KiB, invite.redeem checks the MLS key_package header before spending a use, and redemptions are rate limited per account, invite, channel and server (invite.rejected rate-limited, no use spent). Repeated pending requests are not broadcast again, and a connection with more than 64 MiB queued is terminated (INV-02).

Security (server): federation verifies the signature before spending the nonce, so a bad signature writes nothing. Nonces must be base64url, 16 to 64 chars, with per-origin ceilings on envelopes, key package claims and key-directory fetches. Federation is still off by default (FED-01).
An invite refused for too many requests now shows Error 365 ("Too many invite requests. Wait one minute and try again."). Older clients show "That invite no longer exists." in that case.
Licence: Orwell is now proprietary software (all rights reserved); third-party notices ship with the app and the site (/terceiros.txt). The web build no longer publishes source maps.

Security (server): the server now sees each client's real IP behind the reverse proxy, so per-IP limits (diagnostic reports) apply per person and not to the whole server. Forwarded-for headers sent by clients are ignored (NET-01). Missing files under /app/assets/ now answer 404 instead of the app page.

Call sounds for the moments Discord marks: outgoing ring while you wait for a DM call to be answered, voice connection lost, moved to another room by a moderator, stream started and ended, and someone starting or stopping watching your stream. All synthesized in Orwell's own sound family. Each one has its own toggle in Settings > Notifications > Sounds.

New sound set with a mallet (marimba) timbre and a short room echo. Message, mention, friend online, ringing and nudge have new figures. The update sound has a new figure, so it no longer sounds like friend online.
Being moved to another voice room no longer also plays your own join and the "connected" sound.
Startup animation no longer flashes for a single frame in the browser. It now shows from the first paint, keeps its phase across screens (reduced motion included) and fades out.

Rooms and categories in busy channels no longer flicker (renamed, regrouped, closed or vanishing for a few seconds) when someone joins. A late member re-announcing an older copy of a room can no longer override the newer state on screen.
Deleting a category now sticks in the sidebar. Re-announcements from before the deletion no longer bring it back.
Messages from a previous epoch are attributed using that epoch's tree. Before, a message from someone who had just been removed or re-seated could be dropped, or credited to whoever took their leaf.
When someone joins a channel, members without a role no longer repeat the room list while the channel's admin is still announcing it. One join now sends the rooms once instead of several times.
Server: the common-room join card is accepted up to 8 MiB (it was capped at 256 KiB, about 68 members). Large common rooms accept self-service joins again.

Reduced motion no longer makes the voice halo jump between levels: it still moves in 10% steps, but each step now glides at half speed (180 ms) instead of snapping. Same for the green ring. The universal reduced-motion rule zeroed these transitions; the halo rules now override it.
SFU calls: people re-seated in the channel (new MLS leaf) stayed silent for the rest of the session while shown as connected. Media keys are now looked up by the person's current leaf.

SFU calls: a stream whose media key arrives late waits paused instead of showing as connected while silent. It opens on the next epoch change; until then the call shows "no sound yet" with notice 447.
Sign-up now asks whether to join the Orwell channel (checked by default). You can join later from Communities > "Join the Orwell channel".
Windows installer no longer asks "all users or just me". It always installs per-user and still lets you pick the folder.
Windows: per-machine installs ("all users") receive updates again. Windows asks for permission once.
Leaving the Orwell channel no longer re-joins you on next launch.
Checkbox tick is centered again on Windows.
Remember session: a checkbox on login lets Orwell open next time without asking for your password. On by default. Toggle it in Settings > Account > Session; "Log out" clears it.
Account switching: Settings > Account > Session > "Switch account" keeps the current account on this device and opens another. Each account has its own vault and session.
Desktop: new splash screen and installer.
Desktop: accounts without a password can now set one in Settings > Account > Session. New accounts always get a password.
YouTube embeds in community rooms: thumbnails are now cached, and one room no longer wipes the thumbnails of other rooms.
Desktop: "Log out" on a passwordless account no longer reopens it automatically.
A device removed from a passwordless account no longer prompts for a password that doesn't exist; it shows "Start over" instead.
Desktop: "Switch account", "Delete account" and "Merge accounts" reload the app when done again.
Mic sensitivity: set the threshold below which your mic doesn't transmit, with a live meter. Settings > Voice.
Moderation: "Move to" with nested rooms, and "Disconnect from call". The founder can rename the admin role.
Friend activity alerts: when a friend joins a voice room, starts screen sharing or joins one of your channels. Each alert has its own toggle in Settings > Notifications.
Missed calls: an unanswered private call now shows up in notifications.
When a friend comes online, a toast with their avatar and an "Open chat" button appears in the corner. Auto-dismisses after 2 s.
Notifications open in a window, grouped by day, with All, Mentions, Calls, Invites and Friends filters.
Joining a channel now shows its name, rooms, roles and members right away, even if nobody is online.
Bigger calls: up to 50 people, 4 cameras and 2 screen shares at once.
Near-zero bandwidth when nobody is talking. Voice quality unchanged.
Broken screen share or camera video now recovers in under a second.
When the server is at capacity, new streams get Error 446. Calls already in progress are unaffected.
Game overlay is now off by default (enable it in Settings). Notifications are on by default and sounds at 100%.
Users with the "move" permission can move people without asking them first.
Desktop: notifications no longer show as "blocked by the browser".
Channel names show up again after a page reload.

nota: If you signed up today and don't see the Orwell channel, reload the page. Your account will join automatically.

itens.texto: Screen share at 30 FPS (up from 15).
Since the morning of Nov 2, new accounts couldn't join the Orwell channel. Fixed.

nota: Windows desktop app auto-updates from this version on. If you're on 1.0.6, install 1.0.7 manually one last time.

itens.texto: Desktop game overlay: who's in the room, who's talking and who joins, on top of your game. Drag it wherever you want.
AFK room: muted users in a voice room are moved there automatically, and come back with one click.
Audio sharing: a browser tab, system audio or a window, on top of files.
Fullscreen screen share: corner button or double-click. Esc exits.
Windows desktop app now auto-updates on launch, only to builds we signed.
Per-user call volume: 0 to 200% slider in the user menu.
YouTube thumbnails open the video in a new window, outside the app.
Screen share audio is always included, no checkbox.
Friend online toast auto-dismisses after 2 s.
Voice is prioritized over video on poor connections.
Joining a community with no admin online could leave you without the room list.
Mobile: room list closed when tapping a community whose rooms were still loading.
Browser: viewers of a screen share had no audio until they clicked a button.
Paired device: a new private chat stayed under Communities until the primary device came online.
Safari paired device showed Error 349 and recreated the account wall. The error message no longer exposes the channel address.
Desktop: external links and the outbound filter now check the full URL.

nota: Camera and screen share from 1.0.6 aren't visible on 1.0.5. Please update.

itens.texto: New devices receive history: chats, walls, tickets and files.
Crop your profile picture, channel icon and cover before saving.
Alert when a friend comes online, with their avatar and name.
Short sounds on mute/unmute and deafen.
"LIVE" badge on screen shares, with viewer count.
Desktop: global hotkeys that work while minimized. Any key or mouse buttons 4 and 5.
Messages a device missed while offline are synced, encrypted, from another device on the account.
Ringtone only plays for private messages.
System notifications also show with the window focused, except for the open chat.
Other people's audio dropped when someone joined or left a call.
Screen share showed a partial image.
Two devices on the same account in the same call were using the same keys.
Profiles sync across devices: names show up right away on a new device.
Name changes propagate to all your devices.
Release notes in the "announcements" room of the Orwell channel.
Desktop: sign-up failed with Error 201.
Desktop: "Copy" buttons didn't copy (invites, address, "Add device").
DJ card with track, mute button and volume.
Control panel moved to the bottom of the left column, with bigger buttons.
Clearer wording in Settings.
Rewritten "How Orwell works".
Tickets now show a single warning line.
False error about read receipts.

nota: End of beta. Beta accounts don't carry over to 1.0: create a new account.

itens.texto: The server no longer knows who talks to whom: conversation addresses are encrypted.
"Merge with another account" in Devices.
Wall visible only to friends and people who share a channel with you.
Short invite and friend links: orwell.pt/c#... and orwell.pt/a#...
Invites show the channel name. The server can't see it.
Pairing only deletes the account from this device at the end, and only if everything succeeded.
With "reduced motion" on, animations stopped. They now run slower instead.
End-to-end encryption for chats, channels and calls.
Channels with rooms, roles and tickets. A wall per account.
One account across multiple devices, plus the desktop app.
